title: Randomisation as an assignment mechanism
dek: Randomisation is a known law for Z. It cuts confounding arrows into treatment. It does not make outcomes independent of households, labs, or time.
story: NIST’s first commandment of comparative experiments is randomisation: assign treatments by a known chance mechanism, not by convenience or by who arrived on Tuesday. The statistical object is p(Z | design). Potential outcomes can depend on anything; Z is not allowed to depend on them.

That assignment independence is why a difference in means has a causal reading (under SUTVA). It is not why a GLM SE is right. Clustered outcomes still need clustered SEs or a mixed model. Randomisation of patients inside households does not remove household correlation in Y.

Restricted randomisation (blocks, minimisation, stratified assignment) is still randomisation if the restriction is in the design you analyse. Analysing a blocked experiment as if it were completely randomised throws away precision and can be slightly wrong.
deepTitle: What is randomised, and the analysis that matches
deep: Unit of randomisation should match the intervention: households for a ventilation trial, districts for a policy, patients for a drug. Analysing the wrong level is the ecological/atomistic fork.

Randomisation inference: the null “no effect for anyone” plus the known assignment law gives an exact (or simulation-exact) p-value by permuting Z. That is the permutation plate specialised to a design.

Blinding is not randomisation. It is a measurement-protection against some arrows into the recorded Y. You can randomise without blinding (cluster policy trials) and you can blind poorly after randomising.

Covariate adjustment after randomisation can increase precision. It is not required for unbiasedness of the ITT difference in means. Pre-specify it. Fishing for the covariate that stars the treatment is a different assignment mechanism called the file drawer.

formulas.label: Random assignment (complete, n1 treated)
formulas.expression: P(Z = z) = 1 / C(n, n₁)   for |z|_1 = n₁
formulas.note: A known finite-population assignment law. Stratified versions multiply within strata.

formulas.label: ITT contrast
formulas.note: Effect of assignment. Unbiased for the assignment ATE under the design, plus SUTVA.

example.title: Household ventilation trial
example.setup: 40 households, assign a ventilation kit to 20 by a random partition. Outcome: incident TB over 18 months among members. Temptation: analyse 180 people as iid randomised.

steps.title: Unit
steps.body: Z is a household variable. The assignment law is over 40 labels, not 180.

steps.title: SUTVA
steps.body: Interference between neighbouring households may remain. Within household, members share Z by design — that is clustering, not interference of assignment, if the kit was meant for the house.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.body: Household-level rates, mixed models, or cluster-robust SEs. A person-level t-test uses the wrong p(Z) and the wrong independence.

example.takeaway: Randomise the unit you intervene on. Analyse that assignment law. Correlation in Y is a separate sentence.

check.prompt: Randomisation of treatment Z primarily buys you:
choices: Independent outcomes Yᵢ even within households
Independence (or known dependence) between Z and the potential outcomes, cutting confounding into assignment
check.answer: Independence (or known dependence) between Z and the potential outcomes, cutting confounding into assignment
check.why: Assignment mechanism. Outcome dependence is a different modelling job.

check.prompt: Complete randomisation of n=4 units, n₁=2 treated. Number of possible assignment vectors is C(4,2) =
check.why: 4 choose 2 = 6. Each equally likely under this design. Permutation tests enumerate them.

whyWrong.16: 2^4, unrestricted Bernoulli assignment including 0 or 4 treated.
whyWrong.2: n₁, not the number of assignments.

check.prompt: On the randomisation flow plate, why is “convenience Z” an exit?
check.figureHint: Decision node to randomise vs convenience.
choices: Because convenience assignment is still a known p(Z) like complete randomisation
Because without a known chance mechanism, confounding arrows into Z remain a live scientific problem
check.answer: Because without a known chance mechanism, confounding arrows into Z remain a live scientific problem
check.why: The plate is a design spine. Convenience assignment is observational study in a lab coat.

whyWrong.Because convenience assignment is still: It is not known in the design sense.
whyWrong.Because blocking is convenience: Blocking is restricted randomisation, next plate.
